plan.notes: Source: Official Alvernia University 2025 Academic Completion Plan (formerly 8-semester plan) for BS Computer Science - 'Applies to Students enrolling during the Academic Year beginning in August 2025' - published at https://alvernia.edu/sites/default/files/documents/Computer%20Science_ACP_AY%2025-26.pdf (PDF downloaded to evidence dir and text-extracted via pdftotext; verbatim manual transcription, cross-checked against the PDF layout). Credential honesty: the degree is a B.S. in Computer Science; no substitution. IMPORTANT CATALOG-YEAR NOTE: this is the NEWEST Computer Science completion plan Alvernia publishes. The 2026-27 Academic Completion Plans listing page (https://www.alvernia.edu/8-semester-plans-2024-25, read 2026-09-30) has NO Computer Science entry at all (programs listed run A-Z with no CS link), and no 'Computer Science ACP AY 26-27' PDF is indexed or linked; an official 2026-27 plan exists only for the sibling Artificial Intelligence major. catalog_year is therefore set honestly to 2025-2026, not the current year. TOTAL CREDITS: the ACP prints semester totals of 15/16/15/15/16/15/15/15, summing to 122; the PDF prints NO separate 'Total Credits in Program' line for CS (unlike some other majors). total_credits=122 is the sequence's own published total, used per the Clarkson/UVM/GCSU precedent. Documented discrepancy: Alvernia's general graduation policy requires a minimum of 123 semester credits for a bachelor's degree (per alvernia.edu program pages), so the plan total (122) sits 1 credit under that general minimum - reported honestly, not padded. COMMUNITY SERVICE: the ACP requires 'Complete 5 hours of Community Service' every semester; modeled as 0-credit required milestones (required_zero: true, distinct codes SVC-S1..SVC-S8). DIVERSITY/WRITING-ENHANCED: the ACP header states the Diversity graduation requirement cannot be fulfilled through major courses (fulfill with a Gen Ed SEARCH class) and the Writing Enhanced graduation requirement likewise cannot be fulfilled through major courses. RESIDENCY: students must complete 45 of their last 60 credits at Alvernia. PREREQ CHAINS (official only, nothing invented): CS 155 requires CS 115; CS 220 requires CS 155; CS 310 requires CS 155; CS 320 requires CS 220 AND MAT 230 (per 2024-25 archived undergraduate catalog course descriptions at catalog.alvernia.edu). MAT 230 requires MAT 131 or a satisfactory score on the Math Placement test (per the Alvernia Mathematics program page); the placement-test alternative is documented here, with prereq pointing at the in-plan MAT 131 slot. MAT 209 requires a satisfactory score on the Math Placement test (assessment detail, kept in notes). CS 420 requires junior or senior standing (catalog). Prereqs for AI 101/103/210/220/305, CS 140, CS 162, CS 212, CS 417, MAT 250, SCI 406/407/480 are not published in any official source found - prereq lists left empty rather than invented. CHOICE SLOTS: (1) SRH 101 Search Seminar-Enduring Questions OR HNR 160 Honor Search-Enduring Questions. (2) THE 105 Foundations of Theology and PHI 105 Introduction to Philosophy are both required; the ACP lists 'THE 105 or PHI 105' in BOTH Semester 1 and Semester 2, i.e. take one each semester in either order - modeled as two choice slots with the complementary option. (3) MAT 131 Pre-calculus OR any Gen Ed if MAT 131 is not needed (placement) - choice slot with placement documented; if MAT 131 is not needed, the Semester 6 'Gen Ed (MAT if MAT 131 was not needed)' slot takes a MAT course instead. (4) SCI 406 Research I OR SCI 480 Internship; SCI 407 Research II OR SCI 480 Internship. (5) 'CS Elective' slots (Semesters 6 and 8): any CS elective, options not enumerated officially - empty options list. (6) Generic 'Gen Ed' / 'Gen Ed (Foreign Language suggested)' / 'Gen Ed (Lab Course Suggested)' / 'Elective' slots modeled as student-choice slots with distinct placeholder codes. CAVEAT: the ACP orders some courses across semesters (e.g. CS 162 Database Systems in Semester 2, AI courses woven through) that reflect Alvernia's rotation schedule; students must enroll in the specific courses listed during the semester indicated per Alvernia's ACP policy. Second majors/minors may extend time to degree.
